ranker: absolute affinity model, differences of two predictions
what_this_licenses: An ordering of two peptides of the same series, with the measured accuracy of the similarity band the pair falls in attached, and the applicability condition checked from the two queries. It licenses no numeric affinity estimate, makes no measurement, and creates no knowledge-graph edge. The affinity deployment gate is unchanged and still fails.

cliff_band.note: Pairs above 0.8 mutual similarity are the hardest: a near-identical pair with a real affinity gap is an activity cliff. Their band accuracy is lower than the pooled figure and is quoted in its place, with a warning, rather than letting the pooled number flatter the answer.

findings: Within series, on the domain the service actually serves -- pairs of mutual similarity at least 0.6 differing by at least 0.5 log units -- the ranker is correct on 93.0% of 2730 held-out pairs. Bootstrapping over the 150 held-out molecules those pairs come from, rather than over the pairs, gives a 95% interval of [90.6%, 95.1%]. A binomial bound treating every pair as independent would have claimed 92.0% -- 1.4 points too confident, because a molecule appearing in 16 pairs is one observation, not 16.

Restricting to the served domain matters: over *all* 4166 within-series meaningful pairs the figure is 92.0% with a bound of 89.0%, because cluster co-membership is a looser condition than mutual similarity -- the largest series holds 335 molecules within 0.4 distance of a centroid, so two of its members can be far apart from each other. The quoted figure is the one measured under the condition the service checks.

The ranker also discriminates magnitude: predicted and true differences correlate at Spearman +0.679, so the ordering is not a by-product of knowing a series' position. Accuracy rises with the size of the true difference — 0-0.5 log units: 61.0% of 1714, 0.5-1 log units: 83.8% of 1296, 1-2 log units: 93.7% of 1710, >2 log units: 98.6% of 1160 — which is the behaviour a usable ranker should show.

The hardest calls are between the *most* similar molecules: accuracy falls to 86.2% on 538 pairs above 0.8 similarity, against 94.7% on 2192 pairs between 0.6 and 0.8. A near-identical pair with a real affinity gap is an activity cliff, and the ranker is worst exactly where a chemist most needs it. That is a limitation of the claim, not a reason to withhold it, and it is reported with the answer.

Across unseen series the same ranker reaches 68.5% with a clustered interval of [66.1%, 70.8%] over 375 groups, and magnitude discrimination of +0.157. It fails the same criteria, which is what bounds the claim to within a series rather than leaving it open.

Gate verdict: within-series ranking **passes**; within_series_accuracy_lower_bound = 0.906 against >= 0.8 (met); magnitude_discrimination_spearman = 0.679 against >= 0.3 (met). Passing licenses an ordering with its accuracy attached, not a numeric affinity estimate. The affinity gate is untouched and still fails.
